title: Trent's band heads north and settles in Louisville
summary: The band travels through Memphis, Nashville and Louisville in 1927, where promoter Hurley and musician Lockwood Lewis help them find a roadhouse job.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, that was Alphonso Trent's band. Let's see, do I have anything -- I think I covered the highlights of, you know, most of the guys in the band.

We -- in Trent's band -- we left Little Rock and went our way north, seeking our -- you know, seeking our fortune. You know what I mean? We played Memphis, Tennessee. That's how we (unintelligible) Jimmy Lunceford. We went on and played on around through Jackson, Tennessee; on through Nashville; on up into Louisville, Kentucky.
There was a guy I knew of in Kentucky named Hurley. He was a red cap for Union Station, but he was a band promoter. He promoted all of the bands there at that time. His name was Hurley.

That was 1927. That was '27. And we settled in Louisville with this band. And the guys had their wives -- you know what I mean -- whatnot -- those who were married. So, we set out to look for some, you know, jobs and work.

So, there was a guy -- there was a fellow in town, a musician in town who at one time had been real popular, you know, around town. His name was Lockwood Lewis. Lockwood Lewis. This was a very beautiful man. This was a beautiful
person. Lockwood Lewis helped us get a job in a roadhouse up on the Ohio River. I think that's the Ohio River there in Louisville.
